The fixed_contracts in this file remain the v1-active machine contracts and are NOT asserted to be v2-machine-compliant: the deterministic per-orderId decline, durability-tier declaration, and outcome-split reporting live in scripts/run-e2e-shop-order-saga-baseline.sh and are stamped into run artifacts, not into these static definitions. Per-section v2 enforcement status (implemented-now / partial / deferred) is in scenarios/e2e-shop-order-saga/CONTRACT-v2-IMPLEMENTATION.md. description: End-to-end shop order saga: user registration → graph-based product recommendations → cart operations → order placement → multi-step saga orchestration with compensation
loopback_caveat: Results are not equivalent to network-path benchmarks. transport_mode=loopback-h2c is mandatory in all result artifacts.

concurrency.note: 100 VUs with 800-2500ms think-time between saga steps

neo4j.equivalence_note: Saga orchestration via each platform recommended approach: exeris=flow-native, quarkus=axon-framework (synchronous in request path), spring=axon-framework (async tracking processor, tuned to 16 segments). Not algorithmically equivalent. As of 2026-07-30 all three resolve the terminal outcome INLINE, so end-to-end saga duration is measured identically and order_create_latency_ms is comparison-eligible. spring_runtime_on_exeris_flow_neo4j_h1_v1 remains POLLED and exploratory-only - drivable on this track but not part of the comparison set.

none._note: CONTRACT-v2 §2.1 shape A. The graph was removed from this scenario (§2) because it confounded the only comparison the scenario exists to make, so this track has no graph backend at all — Neo4j is not in the §1 deployment unit and is not started. track_id is an isolation boundary: results here MUST NOT be aggregated with track_a_neo4j.

seed.idempotency_guarantee: Re-running seed.sql produces identical state across users, products, inventory, product_relationships, and user_purchase_history tables. Results without passing pre-run verification are invalid.

workload_invariants.payment_fail_rate_note: All targets participating in cross-runtime comparison MUST be configured with identical payment_fail_rate. Runs where any target deviates from this value are invalid for comparative purposes. Exeris: configured via EXERIS_SAGA_PAYMENT_FAIL_RATE env var. Quarkus/Spring Axon targets: must configure equivalent fail injection via their own mechanism at the same rate.

k6_poll_budget.rationale: 25-attempt budget allows compensation (COMPENSATING state) time to reach terminal COMPENSATED state before marking saga as unresolved

quarkus_axon_neo4j_v1.claim_scope_note: Axon saga targets record end-to-end HTTP latency under the Axon Framework event-sourcing execution model. Request-path DB writes differ structurally from Exeris community (Axon: in-process command dispatch + in-memory SimpleEventBus event publish — no synchronous DB writes in HTTP request path; Exeris: INSERT orders + INSERT order_items + UPDATE saga_id — 3 synchronous DB writes in HTTP request path). Inventory reservation, multi-step saga state transitions, and compensation are not executed in the request path under Axon. Status poll served from in-memory projection (ConcurrentHashMap), not from a DB read. Cross-target latency comparison with exeris-community is NOT supported at this claim scope.
quarkus_axon_neo4j_v1.workload_note: product_level_including_framework: Axon Framework event-sourcing saga model vs Exeris CoreFlowEngine native saga. order_id is a logical AtomicLong saga correlation identifier, not a DB BIGSERIAL row. status_poll_comparison_excluded: true.

spring_runtime_on_exeris_flow_neo4j_h1_v.claim_scope_note: Compatibility-mode hosting: Spring MVC @RestController dispatch is overlaid on the Exeris ingress via ExerisCompatAutoConfiguration (ADR-011). Saga orchestration is exeris-spring-runtime-flow (4 forward steps: reserve-inventory, charge-payment, confirm-order, complete-order; 2 compensations: refund-payment, restore-inventory) — algorithmically the same Flow engine that exeris-community uses, NOT Axon Framework. Synchronous-insert variant: orders + order_items rows are persisted on the request thread before 202 ACCEPTED returns (idempotent under userId + ':' + cartId), so order_create_latency_ms includes JPA-path INSERT cost (unlike the Axon contract, whose request path was DB-write-free). Status poll reads from the JdbcFlowSnapshotStore-backed projection. JPA telemetry bypass disclosure (ADR-017 §6.4): every JPA Connection acquisition flows through the ExerisDataSource compat seam emitting JpaConnectionAcquired + JpaConnectionBound JFR events; cross-target JPA latency / allocation deltas vs kernel-native (exeris-community) or Hikari-pooled (spring-hibernate, quarkus-hibernate) targets must split 'compatibility seam overhead' from 'engine cost'. Protocol-mode mismatch with sibling contracts (this contract H1 plaintext; exeris_community_h2c_v1 and spring_boot_axon_neo4j_v1 are H2C) — direct latency comparison across protocol modes is NOT eligible at strict gate. event_backend = exeris-flow-jdbc-snapshot reflects that there is no external event store: Flow lifecycle state is durably checkpointed by JdbcFlowSnapshotStore (ADR-022), and the workload's outbox writes (in confirm step) target the existing exeris_outbox table directly via JDBC. Spring Boot 3.5.14 line pinned to host-runtime artifact (exeris-spring-runtime:0.5.0-SNAPSHOT) rather than blueprint's SB4 — bench-implementer divergence justified by host-runtime artifact reality (see target README §'Spring Boot matrix alignment').
spring_runtime_on_exeris_flow_neo4j_h1_v.workload_note: saga_engine_identical_to_exeris_community: exeris-spring-runtime-flow uses the same Flow engine class as exeris-community. Hosting axes differ: web ingress = Spring MVC compat overlay on Exeris ingress (this contract) vs Exeris-native ExerisRequestHandler (exeris-community); JPA = ExerisDataSource compat seam (this contract) vs kernel-native QueryExecutor (exeris-community). order_id is a DB BIGSERIAL row id (synchronously persisted), matching exeris-community semantics and differing from the Axon contracts' AtomicLong saga correlation id. status_poll reads from JdbcFlowSnapshotStore projection.
spring_runtime_on_exeris_flow_neo4j_h1_v.equivalence_note: Saga engine identical to exeris_community_h2c_v1 (both run exeris-spring-runtime-flow / Exeris FlowEngine). Differs on hosting axes only: web ingress (Spring MVC compat vs Exeris-native) and persistence path (ExerisDataSource compat seam vs kernel-native QueryExecutor). Against spring_boot_axon_neo4j_v1: same web framework family (Spring MVC), different saga engine (Flow vs Axon) and different host runtime (exeris-spring-runtime compat vs Spring-Boot-on-Tomcat). Both cross-contract comparisons are exploratory; protocol-mode mismatch (H1 here vs H2C on both peers) is the dominant disqualifier for strict-gate latency claims.

exeris_community_h1_v2.protocol_note: h1 because k6 CANNOT drive cleartext HTTP/2 (verified: curl --http2-prior-knowledge and h2load both negotiate h2c against the same endpoint where k6 gets HTTP/1.1; grafana/k6#970 open since 2019). All three targets DO serve h2c, so this is a driver limit, not a target limit. h1-for-all is fair because it is identical on every stack; an h2c track needs a different driver and its own profile key.
exeris_community_h1_v2.resolution_model_note: CONTRACT-v2 section 3 request-response: the POST /api/v1/orders body carries the terminal outcome, so k6 never polls. Uniform across all three contracts as of 2026-07-30 - previously exeris-community and spring-hibernate were polled with 1 s quantization, which made their measured saga duration a flat ~1010 ms of client sleep.
exeris_community_h1_v2.arrival_rate_note: 50 sessions/s chosen from a measured sweep (3/25/50/100/200). 50 is the highest rate clean on ALL stacks: at 100 exeris-community loses its entire measurement phase to connection resets. VU counts are a POOL CEILING under this executor, not concurrency - the previous virtual_users:100 field described a closed-loop model this scenario does not run.
exeris_community_h1_v2.supersedes_note: Supersedes the h2c-named v1 contract for this target. Runs under the two MUST NEVER be aggregated: protocol label, terminal-outcome resolution model and arrival rate all changed.
exeris_community_h1_v2.claim_scope_note: Runs the saga in-process on the request thread and returns the terminal outcome inline. Persists flow state to the Postgres v5 tables, so a share of this stack Postgres cost is saga state - see deployment-footprint.json, which reports it per component. The request thread blocks for the saga duration because FlowScheduler exposes no synchronous execute and no completion handle (section 9(a)).
exeris_community_h1_v2.per_step_metric_claim_scope_note: recommend_latency_ms is platform-natural ONLY: the stacks do NOT issue the same work. quarkus/spring send ONE Cypher query expressing the two-hop join server-side; exeris-community issues 1+N traversals because GraphTraversal (exeris-kernel-spi) carries exactly one GraphEdgeDescriptor and no API accepts a heterogeneous edge path. Measured throughput-matched: 2.6x the Neo4j CPU and 2.5x the latency for exeris. Do not read it as runtime speed. order_create_latency_ms IS eligible now - it was earned by making every stack section-3 compliant, not by relabelling.
exeris_community_h1_v2.workload_shape_note: CONTRACT-v2 §2.1 shape A0: nothing parks. NOT comparison-eligible. The stacks do not execute the same work — quarkus-hibernate runs the whole saga synchronously on the request thread (transaction script), spring-hibernate runs it async via Axon Server, exeris-community via the flow scheduler. All return the terminal outcome inline, but a shared observable contract is not equivalent execution. order_create_latency_ms was briefly lifted to comparison_eligible on 2026-07-30 on the grounds that the RESOLUTION MODEL was uniform; that was wrong and is reverted — resolution uniformity does not imply execution equivalence. Superseded by shape A (minimal park), where every stack must implement dispatch/park/wake and therefore does the same shape of work.

spring_boot_axon_neo4j_h1_v2.claim_scope_note: CORRECTED 2026-07-30. Saga progression IS asynchronous here (event-driven via a tracking processor), unlike quarkus-hibernate which runs the whole saga on the request thread - the two Axon stacks are NOT the same architecture, so the previously shared claim_scope_note was wrong for at least one of them. Two disclosed deviations: (a) the request thread now awaits saga completion so the response carries the terminal outcome per section 3, which is not idiomatic Axon; (d) the saga processor is given 16 segments/threads.
spring_boot_axon_neo4j_h1_v2.tuning_disclosure: CONTRACT-v2 section 9(d): axon.eventhandling.processors.OrderFulfillmentSagaProcessor thread-count=16, initial-segment-count=16. Axon default is ONE segment and ONE thread, which serialized all saga progression and produced 7613 ms median saga latency at 50/s versus 22 ms (exeris) and 34 ms (quarkus). With 16 segments: 37 ms. Comparing a one-thread default against unbounded concurrency measures the default, not the framework. The default-config ceiling is reported separately as its own finding.

quarkus_lra_h1_park1_v3.arrival_rate_note: 50 sessions/s chosen from a measured sweep (3/25/50/100/200). 50 is the highest rate clean on ALL stacks: at 100 exeris-community loses its entire measurement phase to connection resets. VU counts are a POOL CEILING under this executor, not concurrency - the previous virtual_users:100 field described a closed-loop model this scenario does not run.
quarkus_lra_h1_park1_v3.supersedes_note: Supersedes the h2c-named v1 contract for this target. Runs under the two MUST NEVER be aggregated: protocol label, terminal-outcome resolution model and arrival rate all changed.
quarkus_lra_h1_park1_v3.claim_scope_note: CORRECTED 2026-07-30. The previous note (shared verbatim with the spring contract) claimed Axon performs no synchronous DB writes in the HTTP request path. That is FALSE for this stack: AxonOrderSagaCommandHandler.handle runs insert-order, reserve-inventory, charge-payment and confirm-order (or the LIFO compensation pair) synchronously on the request thread and returns the terminal outcome in the POST body. Every domain write happens in the request path here.
quarkus_lra_h1_park1_v3.per_step_metric_claim_scope_note: recommend_latency_ms is platform-natural ONLY: the stacks do NOT issue the same work. quarkus/spring send ONE Cypher query expressing the two-hop join server-side; exeris-community issues 1+N traversals because GraphTraversal (exeris-kernel-spi) carries exactly one GraphEdgeDescriptor and no API accepts a heterogeneous edge path. Measured throughput-matched: 2.6x the Neo4j CPU and 2.5x the latency for exeris. Do not read it as runtime speed. order_create_latency_ms IS eligible now - it was earned by making every stack section-3 compliant, not by relabelling.
quarkus_lra_h1_park1_v3.workload_shape_note: CONTRACT-v2 §2.1 shape A0: nothing parks. NOT comparison-eligible. The stacks do not execute the same work — quarkus-hibernate runs the whole saga synchronously on the request thread (transaction script), spring-hibernate runs it async via Axon Server, exeris-community via the flow scheduler. All return the terminal outcome inline, but a shared observable contract is not equivalent execution. order_create_latency_ms was briefly lifted to comparison_eligible on 2026-07-30 on the grounds that the RESOLUTION MODEL was uniform; that was wrong and is reverted — resolution uniformity does not imply execution equivalence. Superseded by shape A (minimal park), where every stack must implement dispatch/park/wake and therefore does the same shape of work.

terminal_vocabulary._comment: CONTRACT-v2 §3.1 (normative): declared, never inferred. The harness MUST read this and MUST NOT guess either the field or the tokens. quarkus_lra_h1_park1_v3._shape_note: CONTRACT-v2 §2.1 shape A: every stack implements dispatch -> park -> external event -> wake, so for the first time they execute the same SHAPE of work. Graph removed from the scenario (§2). Results under this key MUST NOT be aggregated with shape A0 (…-inline-r50-v2), which was straight-through and is retired.
quarkus_lra_h1_park1_v3._engine_note: quarkus-narayana-lra, official io.quarkus extension, support level PREVIEW. Saga enrolled as ONE participant with the LIFO unwind in application code, because the LRA spec guarantees no ordering across participants. A durable saga ENVELOPE, never 'full LRA' (§9(a)). Runs Quarkus 3.38.2, not 3.34.3.

spring_axon_h1_park1_v3.protocol_note: h1 because k6 CANNOT drive cleartext HTTP/2 (verified: curl --http2-prior-knowledge and h2load both negotiate h2c against the same endpoint where k6 gets HTTP/1.1; grafana/k6#970 open since 2019). All three targets DO serve h2c, so this is a driver limit, not a target limit. h1-for-all is fair because it is identical on every stack; an h2c track needs a different driver and its own profile key.

spring_axon_h1_park1_v3.claim_scope_note: CORRECTED 2026-07-30. Saga progression IS asynchronous here (event-driven via a tracking processor), unlike quarkus-hibernate which runs the whole saga on the request thread - the two Axon stacks are NOT the same architecture, so the previously shared claim_scope_note was wrong for at least one of them. Two disclosed deviations: (a) the request thread now awaits saga completion so the response carries the terminal outcome per section 3, which is not idiomatic Axon; (d) the saga processor is given 16 segments/threads.
spring_axon_h1_park1_v3.tuning_disclosure: CONTRACT-v2 section 9(d): axon.eventhandling.processors.OrderFulfillmentSagaProcessor thread-count=16, initial-segment-count=16. Axon default is ONE segment and ONE thread, which serialized all saga progression and produced 7613 ms median saga latency at 50/s versus 22 ms (exeris) and 34 ms (quarkus). With 16 segments: 37 ms. Comparing a one-thread default against unbounded concurrency measures the default, not the framework. The default-config ceiling is reported separately as its own finding.

spring_axon_embedded_h1_park1_v3.claim_scope_note: Saga progression is asynchronous here exactly as in spring_axon_h1_park1_v3 - the same tracking processor, the same 16 threads/segments s9(d) tuning - but the tokens and saga state are written to Postgres via JPA rather than to Axon Server. The s9(d) disclosure therefore applies unchanged, and one thing it does NOT cover applies only here: the JPA token store takes a row lock per segment per claim, so Postgres carries saga-progression write traffic that the Axon Server shape sends elsewhere. That is the cost this arm is meant to make visible, not a defect.

spring_axon_embedded_h1_park1_v3.deployment_unit_note: TWO processes, against spring_axon_h1_park1_v3's three. Same jar, same saga code, same Axon Framework version; EXERIS_AXON_SERVER_ENABLED=false makes Spring Boot's Axon autoconfiguration fall back to the JPA event store, JpaTokenStore and JpaSagaStore in the SHARED Postgres, with SimpleCommandBus in-process. Registered under CONTRACT-v2 s9(e). It exists because the Axon Server shape hosts part of the saga engine in a container the target-JVM sampler cannot see, so a s8 footprint comparison against in-process saga engines partly measures WHERE the work is hosted rather than what it costs. Both shapes are reported; neither is 'the' Axon number, and the two must never be collapsed into one row.

comparison_disqualifiers: protocol_mode h1 (JDK com.sun.net.httpserver facade, HTTP/1.1 only) vs h2c on the canonical saga contracts — strict-gate disqualifier, same class as spring_runtime_on_exeris_flow_neo4j_h1_v1

CONTRACT-v2 s3 resolution model is INLINE (terminal outcome in the POST /api/v1/orders 200 body, k6 skips the poll loop) whereas exeris-community, spring-hibernate and spring-on-exeris are POLLED with up-to-1s quantization — cross-model saga-duration rows are forbidden without naming each stack resolution model

deployment unit includes an external restate-server container outside the per-process resource sampler; whole-deployment footprint must be attributed separately from logs/restate-server-docker-stats.csv
status poll is an in-memory sticky-terminal projection (status_poll_comparison_excluded), same class as the Axon stacks
restate_saga_h1_park1_v3.durability_tier_note: restate-server 1.7 default = replicated loglet + RocksDB WAL fsync per commit batch (T2 fsync node-durable). CONTRACT-v2 s8 forbids cross-tier comparison; declare the tier per run.
restate_saga_h1_park1_v3.claim_scope_note: Baseline-only per CONTRACT-v2-IMPLEMENTATION.md (restate row) and claim guardrail 4: descriptive single-stack Restate runs are permitted with the durability tier declared; Restate comparisons in tables or prose are NOT, until the disqualifiers above are resolved and the stack is wired as a fixed_contracts entry plus a comparative-pair-manifest row.

restate_saga_h1_park1_v3._promotion_note: PROMOTED from baseline_only_contracts on 2026-08-18: restate is measured alongside spring and quarkus, not kept as a descriptive aside. It qualifies on the same terms as the others — it parks on charge-payment (awakeable resolved by the gateway at the Restate ingress) and it is durable (invocation journal, RocksDB WAL), so §8's cross-tier prohibition does not exclude it.
restate_saga_h1_park1_v3._deviation_9a: The gateway callback resolves the awakeable at the Restate INGRESS and never enters the target JVM — platform-natural, since Restate owns durable execution, but it means this arm's per-callback cost lands in restate-server rather than in the JVM. The whole-deployment footprint still captures it; a target-JVM-only comparison would not.

baseline_only_contracts._note: Contracts that are RUNNABLE but deliberately NOT comparison-eligible. Kept OUT of fixed_contracts and OUT of graph_tracks.*.required_contracts on purpose, so no comparative tooling that walks those two structures can ever pick them up. The saga campaign runner consults this namespace only to derive a --contract-id for a descriptive baseline run, and stamps baseline_only=true on the run. Promotion out of here requires a fixed_contracts entry AND a comparative-pair-manifest.json row AND resolution of the listed disqualifiers.
